name: inverted_index_selection
hypothesis: Iterating the PROMPT once instead of iterating every family's keyword list reduces per-prompt match work from ~909 matchesKeyword calls (40 families * tiered keywords) to ~(prompt-tokens + in-prompt 2-grams) index lookups. Scores remain bit-exact via a keyword->{family,weight} inverted index that aggregates tier contributions per (keyword, family).
mechanism: Registry-load-time build of three structures cached in module scope: (1) singleWord: Map<token, [{family,weight}]> for keywords with no space/dot/slash/dash — matched via a Set of prompt tokens split by /[^a-z0-9_]+/ (mirrors \w word-boundary semantics). (2) multiWord: Map<keyword, [{family,weight}]> for space/dot/slash/dash keywords — scored via substring .includes() prefiltered by a 2-gram prefix bucket (multiWordByPrefix: Map<2char-prefix, keywords[]>) so only keywords whose prefix appears as consecutive chars in the prompt are scanned; this is a sound necessary condition for .includes() match. (3) frameworkLayers: Map<family, layers[]> precomputed, replacing the inner-loop per-family framework layer scan. scoreFamilyTiered and its scoreAllFamilies call graph is replaced with a single pass; fuzzy + semantic fallbacks + smart default preserved unchanged.

scores.note: Medians across 10 full eval runs (363 scenarios each). accuracy + per-corpus figures identical to baseline frontier (0.9945).

testCount.note: 4 failing tests (react-vite validate, fullstack-ts validate, runPromptCorpus e2e, runProofSuite e2e) are pre-existing on main — unchanged by this variant; they fail identically against the baseline selection.ts in this same env.

bitExactScoreParity: Verified with 14,520 (scenario x family) scoring comparisons against legacy scoreFamilyTiered. Zero mismatches.
